title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: approval-synonym rule misses inflected and idiomatic forms
scenario: Round-1 authz#1 fix extended SENSITIVE, but the first pattern still uses bare word forms with \b boundaries (approve|allow|permit|authori[sz]e). \ballow\b cannot match 'allowed' (no boundary between 'allow' and 'ed'), likewise 'permitted' and 'authorized'. APPROVAL_ACTION has no allowed/permitted/green-light/ok-it/ratify/endorse/sanction forms. With a request pending, 'mark the request allowed' or 'make it permitted' or 'green-light the request' or 'ok it' match no SENSITIVE pattern, fall through to make('chat') (voice-intent.ts:147), and reach the local tool-free model via chat(). The model can then answer 'Marked as allowed' with no host action behind it, which is the same truthfulness defect the round-1 finding describes.
fix: Add inflected forms (allowed, permitted, authorized, authorised, approves, grants, granted) and idioms (green light, greenlight, ok it, ratify, endorse, sanction, make it so) to SENSITIVE or APPROVAL_ACTION, and add classifier tests for each.
why:
FIX-INCOMPLETE: confirmed at HEAD b80fab6, src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts. The claim holds as stated, with one line correction.

Evidence:
- Line 43 is the first SENSITIVE pattern: `\b(approve|approved|approving|allow|grant|authori[sz]e|permit|unblock|whitelist)\b`. Because of the trailing \b, "allowed", "permitted", "authorized", "authorised", "grants", "granted" and "approves" do not match. "allow"/"authorize" are followed by a word character, so no boundary exists.
- APPROVAL_ACTION (line 67) has no allowed, permitted, authorized, green light, greenlight, ok it, ratify, endorse or sanction forms. Its "ok to" / "okay to" forms do not cover "ok it".
- Line 165 is the fall-through `return make("chat")`. Line 147 is the SENSITIVE check, so the claim's line citation for the fall-through is slightly off. The behavior is the same.
- Traced "mark the request allowed", "make it permitted", "green-light the request" and "ok it" (normalized to "it" after FILLER strips the leading "ok") through every classifier branch, with proposalPending both true and false. None matches SENSITIVE, CONFIRM, CANCEL, OPEN_UI, STATUS, VERIFY, MODEL, APPROVALS, LAST_MISSION, CONTROL or REDIRECT, so each returns kind "chat".
- voice-session.server.ts:661 routes "chat" to chat() (line 809). That builds a tool-free prompt for the local model and speaks the answer. No host action follows, so the model can speak a false "Marked as allowed" while the proposal stays pending on screen. That is a truthfulness defect with limited impact, and it breaks the "sensitive requests refused" invariant for these phrasings.
- voice-intent.test.ts has no case for allowed, permitted, authorized, green-light or ok it. Only "allow this command" appears in the test file.

Why not lower: the spoken-chat path is the one the round-1 authz#1 finding targeted, and the stated invariant is that sensitive requests are refused, not routed. Why not higher: no execution, approval or identity authority is granted by the chat route (it is tool-free, and confirm/cancel are gated separately), so the impact is a misleading spoken answer, not an exploitable action.

Suggested fix as in the claim: add the inflected forms and idioms to the SENSITIVE or APPROVAL_ACTION sets, and add classifier tests for each.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: worker integrity still treats the release manifest as optional and self-attests from the committed build record

At HEAD verifyWorkerIntegrity reads binarySha256 and sourceSha256 from native/voice/bunny-voice-worker.json, which is itself a committed, unsigned file, and only checks the release manifest when it exists (if (existsSync(manifestPath))). A tree containing a replaced exe, a matching rewritten record and no manifest passes the check and is spawned. This is the same-user writer class that the disclosed residual places out of contract, but the packaged-path requirement was not implemented.

title: Over-refusal: approval-synonym rule refuses plain questions that use enable/accept with 'it'
scenario: The new APPROVAL_ACTION x APPROVAL_TARGET rule pairs 'enable' or 'accept' with a bare 'it', 'one', or 'this' within 30 characters. A harmless question such as 'how do I enable it' or 'can you accept the one I wrote earlier' is classified sensitive_refused and answered 'Not allowed by voice' instead of being answered as chat. This is a truthfulness and usability defect, not an authority bypass.
fix: Narrow the rule so the approval target is an approval-like noun (approval, permission, request, pending, proposal) rather than a bare pronoun, or allow question forms ('how do I', 'can you explain') to fall through to chat, and add tests for both.
why: The core mechanism holds at HEAD b80fab6. The approval-synonym rules are at src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-intent.ts:67-70, not line 43 (line 43 is the first generic approve/allow regex). APPROVAL_ACTION (line 67) includes enable/enabled/enabling and accept/accepting. APPROVAL_TARGET (line 68) includes bare it/that/this/one/all. Lines 69-70 push both orderings onto SENSITIVE with a 30-character gap, and classifyTranscript (voice-intent.ts:147) runs SENSITIVE before every other class. So "how do i enable it" and "can you accept the one i wrote earlier" are classified sensitive_refused. voice-session.server.ts:627-630 then speaks REFUSAL_TEXT, which is "I can't do that by voice. Approvals, permissions and commands are reviewed on the Windows Host screen." (voice-session.server.ts:34). The claim's quoted "Not allowed by voice" is wrong. Ordering is fail-closed, so no authority is granted and no invariant is broken. The defect is a usability and truthfulness problem: benign questions get an approval refusal. That fits LOW (hardening/over-refusal), not MEDIUM. The suggested fix (narrow the target to approval-like nouns, or let question forms fall through) is reasonable. Note that the rule also catches "agree/proceed/accept with it" in harmless questions, which is the same defect class.

So "how do i enable it" and "can you accept the one i wrote earlier" both match within 30 characters and return sensitive_refused. voice-model.ts:211 maps sensitive_refused to "Not allowed by voice", so a benign question gets a refusal label. This is an over-refusal and a truthfulness/usability defect only. No invariant allowing execution or control is broken, since refusal is the fail-closed direction and the rule only narrows what reaches chat. The 30-character window also catches "accept all the notes" and "enable this setting" style chat. Severity LOW matches the rubric's hardening/usability tier; it is not MEDIUM because the refusal does not mislead about any control state. The suggested fix (require approval-like nouns or question-form exemptions, plus tests) is reasonable.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: approval phrasings outside the synonym list still reach the local chat model

title: Command-execution requests without a listed noun route to the tool-free chat model, which can answer as if done
scenario: The SENSITIVE 'run/execute' pattern (line 44) requires one of a fixed noun list (command, shell, script, code, npm, git, python, node, rm, curl, installer...). 'run the tests', 'run the build', 'restart the server', 'kill the process', 'install the package' and 'reboot the machine' match no SENSITIVE, control, status or redirect pattern, so they are classified 'chat' and admitted to the local model. The sensitive-requests-refused invariant treats commands as sensitive, yet these are answered by the model rather than refused. Because the model is tool-free and its prompt has no 'you cannot act' instruction, it may spoken-claim completion (for example 'All tests passed') with no Host action behind it.
fix: Broaden the execution rule to any imperative execution verb (run, execute, restart, kill, install, reboot, build, test, deploy, start, stop-the-machine) with a machine or project object, or make the chat prompt state that Bunny cannot run or change anything and must say so, then add classifier tests for these phrasings.

title: Spoken 'cancel' answers 'Okay, cancelled.' while the named agent keeps running

title: Closing the Island does not close a session whose open or listen.start is still queued or in flight
scenario: A hotkey press queues voice.session.open and voice.listen.start. The Island window closes before the open response lands. Add_Closing sends voice.session.close only when $script:bunnyVoiceOpenPolling is true, and that flag is set from the last snapshot (line 281), so it is still false. No close is sent. If listen.start was already in flight, the Host starts a capture (source hotkey, VAD endpoint) with no Island attached, and it runs up to 30 s. In push_to_talk mode there is no idle close on the Host, so the session and its worker stay open after the Island exits.
fix: In Add_Closing, send voice.session.close whenever a voice.session.open or voice.listen.start is queued or in flight, not only when the last snapshot says open. Close is idempotent on the Host.

- Host side: push_to_talk has no idle close. armIdle (voice-session.server.ts:1282) is armed only at line 389 for hands_free or source hands_free. A PTT session opened and never closed persists with its worker until a close or Host restart.

- The scenario "listen.start already in flight, flag still false" is reachable only in a sub-100 ms window. Invoke-BunnyVoicePump is also called synchronously from Add-BunnyVoiceRequest (line 75). If that pump applies the open response and starts the listen.start flight inside an event handler, the flag is not updated until the next tick. A Closing event landing in that gap sends no close, and listen.start then reaches the Host. With source hotkey, that gives VAD endpointing and up to 30 s capture (voice-session.server.ts:386-387) with no Island visible.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE: recognizer engine leaks when StartRecognizer throws, bypassing the abandon ledger
scenario: CaptureTurn.StartRecognizer assigns engine = new SpeechRecognitionEngine(...) at line 1129, then calls LoadGrammar(new DictationGrammar()) at 1130 and RecognizeAsync at 1143. If either throws (for example on a machine with an en-US recognizer but no dictation support), Program.StartCapture (lines 2753-2757) closes only the WaveInSource, emits STT_UNAVAILABLE and returns. The CaptureTurn that owns the engine is dropped. The engine is never disposed and is never added to AbandonLedger, so the ledger cap of 2 does not cover it. Each push-to-talk attempt that hits this path leaks one SAPI recognizer engine, so the resource growth is unbounded per user action.
why: Real but overstated. At HEAD native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1129 creates the SpeechRecognitionEngine, and lines 1130 (LoadGrammar) and 1143 (RecognizeAsync) can throw with no try/catch or Dispose. StartCapture (2751-2758) closes only the source, emits STT_UNAVAILABLE, and returns, so the engine is never disposed. The claim's facts are accurate. Two parts are overstated. (1) The ledger is not bypassed in any way that matters: AbandonLedger (1438-1470) caps engines still running after a finalize timeout, and a start-failed engine never began recognition, so it does not occupy a running slot. (2) "Unbounded per user action" is too strong: the failed CaptureTurn is unreferenced, so the engine and its native handles are only reclaimed by GC/finalization rather than held forever. Growth is GC-bounded, and it needs a machine-specific failure (for example no dictation support). This is a resource-hygiene gap in the same class as the round-1 native2 fix, which covered only the timed-out path, so it is a legitimate incomplete-fix hardening item. The suggested fix (dispose the engine on any post-construction failure) is correct. Severity LOW under the rubric, not MEDIUM, since no listed invariant is broken exploitably by default and the leak is bounded by GC.

Claim does not hold exactly as stated. The engine is not in AbandonLedger, so the cap of 2 does not cover it. Because `Active` is only set after StartRecognizer succeeds, nothing else is affected.

The overstated part is the impact. The "unbounded per user action" and MEDIUM claims are not supported. If LoadGrammar throws, RecognizeAsync never ran, so the engine has no audio input, no capture thread and no recognition in flight. What remains is an undisposed SAPI engine object, which is reclaimed only by GC finalization. The growth is therefore GC-bounded, not strictly per action. Nothing in the code shows an unbounded leak, and I could not verify a finalizer chain offline.

title: Timed-out playback chunk leaks its PCM and header buffers, and the device handle when waveOutClose fails
scenario: In PlayReal, when the device is still not done after c.AudioMs*2+3000 ms and again after the 1000 ms wait, the code calls ReleaseDone(c), which only releases when IsDone is true. It then calls CloseDevice(), which runs waveOutReset and waveOutClose and sets waveOut and handle to null regardless of the result. Nothing calls Release or FreeChunk for the chunk, so c.Header and c.Data (up to about 1 MB of PCM for a 400-character chunk) are never freed. If waveOutClose returns WAVERR_STILLPLAYING because the headers are still prepared, the device handle is also dropped while still open. Each stalled driver therefore leaks one chunk, and repeated stalls accumulate. This is a leak, not a use-after-free: the driver is reset before the buffers are abandoned.
why: Claim holds at HEAD b80fab6, with narrower impact than the scenario implies. Evidence from native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs (scratch copy of HEAD): PlayReal timeout branch at ~1981-1990 calls h.Reset(), waits up to 1000 ms, then ReleaseDone(c) (releases only if IsDone), then CloseDevice() (line 1895: Reset + Close, sets waveOut=null), then FailAndDrop. WaveOut.Close (~819-829) sets handle to zero without checking the waveOutClose result. Release/FreeChunk (~802-814) are reached only on the done path, and nothing else frees inFlight. So if the header is still not done 1 s after waveOutReset, the chunk's Header and Data are leaked, and if waveOutClose returns WAVERR_STILLPLAYING the handle is dropped while open. Mitigating factors: waveOutReset normally returns all pending headers as WHDR_DONE, so the leak needs a hung driver that ignores reset. Not freeing an undone header is also the safe ordering, because freeing it would be a use-after-free, so the suggested fix must defer the free until IsDone rather than free immediately. The per-stall size figure in the claim was not verified. Severity LOW matches the rubric's hardening tier: a bounded leak per hung-driver stall, reclaimed when the worker process exits (it runs in the F04 Job Object and is restarted with the Host), with no invariant broken by default.

- PlayReal timeout branch (about lines 1982-1991): after h.Reset() and a 1000 ms wait, the code calls ReleaseDone(c), which releases only if h.IsDone(c) (line 2003-2005). It then calls CloseDevice() and returns false. Nothing else frees c.Header or c.Data on this path.
- FreeChunk is reached only via Release (line 805), Submit's two failure branches (lines 789, 796), and Release's own path. Release is called only from ReleaseDone (line 2005). The null-sink Release at line 2174 is a no-op. The chunk is removed from the queue at line 1855 and not retained, so nothing else owns the HGlobal buffers. The leak is real.
- WaveOut.Close (lines 819-829) ignores the waveOutClose result and sets handle to zero, so a WAVERR_STILLPLAYING return drops the open handle. This is also real.
- Refutation attempts that failed: there is no use-after-free, because the driver is reset before the buffers are abandoned and the header memory is not freed. A chunk is capped at 400 characters (MaxChunkChars, line 1521), so the leak is about 1 MB per stall at most, which is consistent with the claim.
- Severity: the trigger requires a driver that does not mark the header done within about 1 s of waveOutReset. waveOutReset normally completes pending headers immediately, so this needs a hung or faulty audio driver. Each stall leaks one chunk, and the process does not reclaim it. That is a bounded-resources hardening defect, LOW.

title: FIX-INCOMPLETE-adjacent: raw microphone buffers are freed without being zeroed
scenario: WaveInSource.Read copies each captured frame from the unmanaged waveIn buffer into the managed frame array. Close() then frees the unmanaged data[] buffers with Marshal.FreeHGlobal at line 680 without zeroing them. The managed frame and fed arrays in CaptureLoop are also not cleared. The Pipe path is zeroed (PcmPipe.Wipe uses Array.Clear), so the wipe is inconsistent. Raw microphone audio therefore remains in freed heap memory and in unzeroed managed arrays after the turn ends, which weakens the 'no raw audio retained' invariant. It is in-process only, with no disk or network write.
why: Verified at HEAD b80fab6 (read-only, via git show). The core fact holds: WaveInSource.Close() (native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:665-683) calls Marshal.FreeHGlobal(data[i]) at line 680 with no zeroing of the six unmanaged waveIn capture buffers, and CaptureLoop (lines 1183-1184, 1196, 1224-1225) never clears its managed frame and fed arrays on exit. The asymmetry with PcmPipe.Wipe (lines 886-890, which does Array.Clear before releasing the turn audio, called at line 1391 in the finalize finally) is real. Two parts of the claim are overstated or mis-cited. First, the claim cites PcmPipe.Wipe at 899-901; the zeroing is actually at 886-890. Second, the scope is much narrower than "raw microphone audio remains after the turn ends". The full buffered turn audio, which is the actual retention concern, is zeroed by Pipe.Wipe. What remains unzeroed is at most the six waveIn ring buffers (overwritten continuously by the driver while capturing) plus one raw frame and one fed frame, all in-process, with no disk or network path. That is a bounded hardening gap, consistent with the claim's own LOW rating. Not a round-1 re-report and not a FIX-REGRESSION, since the round-1 pipe wipe fix is intact.

Skeptic #2 review of the claimed defect at HEAD b80fab6, native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs.

The claim holds as stated, with a caveat on its framing:
- WaveInSource.Close (lines 665-683): the unmanaged data[i] buffers are released with Marshal.FreeHGlobal at line 680 with no zero-fill first. Raw microphone samples captured into those buffers are therefore left in freed heap memory. This is confirmed.
- WaveInSource.Read (lines 648-662): the frame array is Array.Clear'd before the copy, but the source buffer itself is never cleared.
- CaptureLoop (around lines 1181-1270): frame and fed are plain managed arrays. The finally block (around line 1270) only calls source.Close(). Neither array is cleared on exit, so raw samples persist in unreferenced managed memory until the GC reuses it. This is confirmed.
- PcmPipe.Wipe (lines 886-895) does Array.Clear on its own buffer, and Pipe.Wipe() is called at line 1391. So the inconsistency is real.

Why severity stays LOW and is not higher: the "no raw audio retained" invariant is about retention by the system (disk, network, logs, persisted state). The residue here is in-process and transient, and is only reachable by reading this worker's own process memory, which is already in the same trust domain. There is no disk or network write, which the claim itself concedes. Under the rubric this is hardening, not an exploitable invariant break.

Suggested fix is sound: zero each data[i] (or Marshal.Copy zeros) before FreeHGlobal, and Array.Clear frame and fed in a finally in CaptureLoop.

title: Blocking stdout writes run while holding Speaker.gate and Program.Gate
scenario: Several Out.Emit calls run inside lock(gate) in the Speaker: playback.started at 1967 (PlayReal), chunk_done at 1997, playback.idle at 1859 (PlayStep), tts.ready at 1758 and playback.error at 1752 (SynthStep), and the FailAndDrop emit at 2011. StartCapture emits capture.started under Program.Gate at about line 2762. Out.Emit blocks in stream.Write when the host has stopped draining the stdout pipe. While it is blocked the playback thread holds Speaker.gate, so Speaker.Cancel (speak.cancel / barge-in) cannot acquire the gate and the command loop stalls behind it. Already-submitted audio then keeps playing until the host resumes reading. This needs the host to stop draining stdout for a long time, so it is a defense gap, not a routine failure.
why: Claim verified at HEAD b80fab6 (native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs). Line facts are accurate: PlayReal emits playback.started at 1967 and playback.chunk_done at 1997 inside lock(gate) (1962, 1994); PlayStep emits playback.idle at 1859 inside lock(gate) (1851); SynthStep emits tts.ready at 1758 and playback.error at 1752 under lock(gate) (1740); FailAndDrop emits at 2011 and is called under gate. Out.Emit (219-245) holds the static Lock around stream.Write plus Flush, so a blocked stdout write holds the caller's gate. Speaker.Cancel (1624-1660) takes lock(gate) as its first action, and CancelSpeech runs on the command loop via Dispatch, so the command loop does stall on speak.cancel. The StartCapture emit at 2762 is inside lock(Gate) (2732), which blocks the capture.start/abort/mute paths that take Program.Gate. The claim is therefore exact as to mechanism. Mitigating context: the host reads stdout in a Node 'data' handler and its framer drops overfull buffers rather than stopping the read (voice-worker.server.ts:111, 234), so the stall needs the host event loop itself to hang. Also, Out.Lock already serializes all emitters, so a blocked write stalls the command loop's next Emit regardless of gate, and barge-in cannot reset the device while the playback thread is blocked in Emit either. The gate-hold therefore adds limited incremental harm. This is a liveness and hardening gap, not an exploitable default defect, so LOW fits the rubric.

Refuted as stated. The code pattern exists at HEAD b80fab6: Out.Emit inside lock(gate) at native/voice/BunnyVoiceWorker.cs:1967 (PlayReal playback.started), :1997 (chunk_done), :1859 (PlayStep playback.idle), :1752/:1758 (SynthStep), :2011 (FailAndDrop, called from :1957 under gate and :1990). capture.started is emitted inside lock(Gate) at :2762 (lock opened at :2732), and CaptureError emits at :2734-2737 are also inside that lock. Out.Emit writes under Out.Lock (:237-240), so the nesting is real. However the claimed causal chain does not hold. While stdout is stalled, the playback thread is blocked inside stream.Write holding Out.Lock. Any Cancel path that reaches its receipt Emit (Cancel at :1641 returns to the caller and the receipt is emitted outside gate) blocks on Out.Lock regardless of whether Speaker.gate is held, so the command loop stalls in both designs. The device reset is applied only on the playback thread (ApplyPendingReset, :1891 area), which is itself stuck in the write, so audio cannot be stopped in either design while stdout is stalled. The only delta from moving emits outside gate is a narrow ordering race (a Cancel that could mark queued chunks before the playback thread's next PlayStep), which is a hardening nicety, not an invariant break. Because the stated impact (audio keeps playing until host resumes reading, command loop stalls) occurs identically without the lock nesting, I find no defect attributable to the gate ordering. Optional LOW hardening remains (emit after releasing gate, as the Cancel path already does), but it is not a concrete defect at HEAD.

title: Worker integrity manifest check is optional, contradicting the packaging claim
scenario: verifyWorkerIntegrity() (lines 59-69) consults release-manifest.json only `if (existsSync(manifestPath))`. A release folder with that file removed skips the manifest check entirely, so the Host launches the worker on the self-consistency check alone. scripts/package-bunny-desktop.ps1 line 82 says the Host 'refuses to launch it unless the release manifest lists the same sha256', which the code does not do. An actor who can write the release folder can swap bunny-voice-worker.exe and rewrite the matching .json record (and the manifest entry, if present) and the check still passes. The record's sourceSha256 is compared only to the working-tree .cs, not to the manifest. Impact is bounded because the attacker needs same-user write access to the release folder, which the F04 contract places out of scope, and the Bunny-A launcher pins the manifest hash when it is used.
fix: Require the manifest in release mode (throw WORKER_INTEGRITY when release-manifest.json is absent but the worker lives under a release root), and verify the record and source hashes against their manifest entries too. Or correct the packaging comment so it does not claim a guarantee the code does not provide.
why:
Title: Worker integrity manifest check is optional, contradicting the packaging claim (claim holds as stated, verified at HEAD b80fab6).

Evidence:
- src/lib/bunny-host/voice/voice-worker.server.ts:59-69: `const manifestPath = join(root, "release-manifest.json"); if (existsSync(manifestPath)) {...}`. If the file is absent, the function returns at line 70 having checked only the exe hash against the build record (lines 52-53) and the .cs hash against the record's sourceSha256 (lines 55-58). The manifest entry is never consulted.
- scripts/package-bunny-desktop.ps1:82 says "The Host refuses to launch it unless the release manifest lists the same sha256." The code does not enforce this.
- The in-code doc comment at line 38 ("A release manifest, when present, must list the same hash") is accurate, so the defect is the packaging comment overclaiming, not a hidden bypass in the code.
- The build record (bunny-voice-worker.json) is self-consistent with the exe and the .cs, so a writer who controls the folder can rewrite exe, record and source together and pass the check. The only manifest-independent anchor is the record itself.

Mitigations (why not HIGH): the attacker needs same-user write access to the release folder, which the F04 contract places out of scope (disclosed residual). The Bunny-A install path pins the manifest hash (scripts/install-bunny-release.ps1:150 stores manifestSha256; the launcher reads the manifest at install/Bunny-A-Windows-Launcher.cs:82), so removing or rewriting the manifest is caught there when that launcher is used. The Host's own launch path (launchVoiceWorker, line 324 and 336) does not reach that pin.

Severity: the defect is real and the impact is a truthfulness and defense-gap issue with limited reach, which fits MEDIUM under the rubric. The fix is either to require the manifest in release mode and verify record and source against it, or to correct the packaging comment. I did not run any tests or builds, as instructed.

The release is launched only through install/Start-Bunny-Release.ps1, which first checks release-manifest.json against the manifestSha256 anchored in install.json (Start-Bunny-Release.ps1:9). title: Voice approvals answer omits agents waiting on consent (authorization WAITING_FOR_USER)

The existing test at voice-answers.test.ts:123 only exercises agent.state, so it does not catch the gap.
fix: Count an agent when authorization?.state === 'WAITING_FOR_USER' (and keep the agent.state rule if it is also a real approval), with a test where state is RUNNING and authorization.state is WAITING_FOR_USER and the answer names that agent.

- The consent proposal (agentic-store.server.ts:88, via manager.server.ts:2077) is normally made on a mission in "ready", which derives agent WAITING_FOR_USER (agent-types.ts:160), so the first-consent path is usually covered.
